answer: Each agent identity must anchor itself by solving a sequential cipher puzzle chained to its public key before it can transact. The puzzle cannot be parallelized: one CPU core needs about six hours to forge a valid proof, while verification takes milliseconds. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake identities must therefore burn 6,000 CPU-hours, while an honest agent pays the cost once. The anchor record is public, so any peer can recheck the proof without trusting the claimant, and a forged proof is rejected instantly.
